news.headline: Physical activity may protect against depression for people at genetic risk
news.summary:
Denver Brown, in kinesiology, studies whether physical activity protects against depression.
The work looks especially at people with a genetic risk for depression.

news.headline: NIH asks for ideas to reduce administrative burden in grants
news.summary:
NIH is asking researchers and research administrators where its grant requirements add work without adding value.
Comments can cover steps to simplify or drop, duplicated requirements, unclear rules, and reports that are collected but never used.
Early Stage Investigators and smaller institutions are named as groups that may carry more of the burden.
Responses are due December 8, 2026, through the NIH request-for-information portal.
NIH may post responses publicly, so leave out unpublished or sensitive details.

news.headline: K-State members can search for funding with Atom Grants
news.summary:
K-State now provides Atom Grants, a tool that matches researchers to funding opportunities from a plain-language description of their work.
It sends weekly emails about matching opportunities and lists each announcement's key requirements.
Sign in at atomgrants.com with your eID@ksu.edu address, at no cost.

news.headline: National Institutes of Health proposes broader safety monitoring for clinical research
news.summary:
The National Institutes of Health released a draft update to its policy on data and safety monitoring.
The draft would extend monitoring plans from clinical trials to all clinical research it funds, including behavioral studies and other studies with human participants.
Each study would need a risk-based monitoring plan that the funding institute approves before work with participants begins.
Comments are due January 6, 2027.

news.headline: National Science Foundation updates its Major Research Instrumentation program
news.summary:
The National Science Foundation released a new announcement for the Major Research Instrumentation program (NSF 27-500).
The 2027 cycle has two submission windows, January 4 to 29 and October 18 to November 19.
Only the three K-State teams chosen in this fall’s internal competition may submit in January.
The Office of Research Development will explain its process for the November round early in 2027.

news.headline: K-State News features Stephanie Hall’s research on exercise and Alzheimer’s disease
news.summary:
Stephanie Hall, assistant professor of anatomy and physiology in the College of Veterinary Medicine, studies whether exercise can prevent or delay Alzheimer’s disease.
Her work focuses on risk factors that can be changed, such as blood pressure, cholesterol, and depression.
The story explains why early stages matter, since changes in the brain can begin about 20 years before symptoms.

news.headline: K-State biologists identify a signal that helps cells start making proteins at unusual sites
news.summary:
Katsura Asano, professor in the Division of Biology, and his team found a short genetic sequence that helps cells begin making proteins at alternative start sites.
They also studied a protein that holds this process in check.
The work matters for cancer and for some neurodegenerative diseases, including forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
The study was published in Science Advances in November 2026.

news.headline: Carl Ade named K-State’s Big 12 Faculty of the Year
news.summary:
Carl Ade, associate professor in the School of Health Sciences and associate director of CNAP, is K-State’s 2026–27 Big 12 Faculty of the Year honoree.
His research covers heart stress, heart damage from chemotherapy, and how spaceflight affects the body.
He directs the Clinical Integrated Physiology Lab and leads research teams of undergraduate and graduate students.

news.headline: K-State’s infectious disease center earns $11.4 million for its second phase
news.summary:
The National Institutes of Health approved $11.4 million for the second phase of the Center on Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases in the College of Veterinary Medicine.
Like CNAP, the center is funded through the Centers of Biomedical Research Excellence program.
In its first phase, the center’s researchers earned 21 awards totaling about $9 million.
The new phase runs through April 30, 2031.

news.headline: Early results from a shared school and nursing home point to gains for both generations
news.summary:
K-State researchers reported first-year results from a rural Kansas building that houses both an elementary school and a nursing home.
Residents’ thinking skills held steady, their depressive symptoms fell, and they became more independent in daily tasks.
Children gained in social and emotional development and in reading and math scores.
The results are preliminary.

news.headline: Erika Geisbrecht’s lab studies how muscle disease develops
news.summary:
Erika Geisbrecht, professor of biochemistry and molecular biophysics, studies inherited muscle diseases and how muscles form and are maintained.
A graduate student in her lab found that a faulty muscle protein forms clumps that cells push out rather than break down.
She received the Commerce Bank and W.T. Kemper Foundation Distinguished Graduate Faculty Award in spring 2026.
